question: before any agent code: what can each tool do to the world, and what flows back into the agent's context from each?

planted.what: lookup_order returns gift_message and delivery_instructions, free text the shopper typed. That is attacker-shapeable content flowing into the agent's context, so it needs an injection case, the same as the carrier page from fetch_tracking. Treating lookup_order as a trusted internal lookup misses it.
cancel_order, issue_refund and send_email are one-way. Each needs its own confirmation or refusal case; a yes for one call does not cover the next.

All merchants' sessions share workers and a database. The design must state a checkable boundary: one merchant's (and one shopper's) orders and tool results never reach another session's context, and every tool is scoped by merchant_id.

traps.what: A single human approval that covers all one-way actions in a session (approve once, then the agent refunds, cancels and emails freely).
must_not_say_any: one human approval for the session
